ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory customer due diligence under Luxembourg AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004; all UBOs and managers must be screened against PEP databases, FATF-recognized PEP definitions, EU consolidated financial sanctions lists, UN Security Council sanctions, OFAC SDN list for USD transactions, and domestic sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for non-resident UBOs, politically exposed persons, complex ownership chains, and any unusual source-of-funds indicators. Findings must be documented in an audit trail and reportable to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (Cellule de renseignement financier).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Luxembourg Online Portal and MyGuichet.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The name must be expressed in Latin script. Official administrative languages are French, German, and Luxembourgish. If the proposed corporate group uses a non-Latin script, a certified transliteration into Latin script and a French, German, or English translation must be filed. The corporate name must include the required legal-form designation 'Société en commandite spéciale' or 'SCSp'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The law firm must file a written reconsideration request with the RCS/LBR within 30 days of a refusal, explaining the lawful basis and supplying alternative supporting evidence. If reconsideration is refused, an administrative appeal may be lodged before the Luxembourg Tribunal administratif within 3 months from notification. No longer extension of the initial 30-day reservation is available; a fresh name availability check may be filed after the refusal process.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Domiciliation through a Luxembourg registered-office and domiciliation agent is permitted for the SCSp structure; however, a pure virtual mailbox without a physical Luxembourg location is not acceptable for a licensed immigration-visa advisory activity. The undertaking must have a physical place where client files, UBO/KYC records, corporate books, and accounting records are available for inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 70% high likelihood; unannounced on-site inspections are expected because the business purpose is a licensed international student placement and immigration visa residence advisory service carrying enhanced AML/CFT obligations and ongoing supervision by the competent Luxembourg administrative authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 932-1 to 932-25 introducing the Special Limited Partnership via the Law of 23 July 2016); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies; Law of 2 September 2011 on the Exercise of Commercial Activities; Law of 13 January 2019 on the Register of Beneficial Owners
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de Société (Partnership Deed / Articles of Association) filed via LBR e-filing portal and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SCSp under Article 932-3 of the 1915 Law; contributions in cash, kind or industry permitted; no compulsory escrow account at incorporation, but client funds held for visa/immigration mandates must be segregated in an escrow or client account under the AML/CFT Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF prudential guidance
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED BY THE GENERAL PARTNER: (1) The subscription lists and capital contributions of the initial partners are ratified; the allotment of partnership interests is approved per the Subscription Schedule; (2) The registered office of the Société en Commandite Spéciale is fixed at [ADDRESS], Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; the General Partner is authorized to execute the lease and effect registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax administration and Chamber of Commerce; (3) [NAME] is appointed Gérant (Manager) with full powers to operate the study-abroad and immigration-visa advisory business, open bank accounts and represent the SCSp; (4) The General Partner and Manager are authorized to file all applications for the state business establishment permit and professional accreditations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS online search portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability query through the LBR e-search module for the proposed SCSp corporate name, ensuring no identical or confusingly similar commercial name exists in the RCS; no separate fee is charged for the pre-check; the name is definitively protected upon filing of the partnership deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (maximum two competing alternatives)
Description of the entity type (SCSp)
Identification details of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or conflicts with an existing registration, file a new name query with a revised corporate name; no substantive cure procedure exists beyond renaming.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the partnership deed (Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (if real estate contribution) or private deed executed by the general partner; advised by a Luxembourg corporate counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Contrat de Société in Luxembourg law, including the SCSp's legal form election, registered office address, purpose clause covering student placement and immigration visa advisory services, contribution schedules, capital and profit-sharing provisions, and the appointment of the first manager (Gérant); execute the deed by private signature with advanced electronic signature where no notarial deed is statutorily required.
required_dossiers: Constitutional draft partnership deed
Valid passport or national ID and proof of address of each partner
Curriculum vitae and criminal record extract for the proposed manager
Statement of subscription and contribution in-kind report (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel raises legal-form deficiencies, amend the draft deed by addendum prior to signature; re-execution costs are borne by the instructing partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the client escrow and operating bank account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution chosen by the general partner (e.g. BGL BNP Paribas, BCEE, Banque Internationale à Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed partnership deed, proof of RCS registration intent and full KYC packs of the general partner, manager, and ultimate beneficial owners; open a segregated client escrow account for visa application funds and a separate operating account for the SCSp's consulting fees; deposit any agreed initial contributions.
required_dossiers: Notarized or private-deed copy of the partnership deed
KYC/documentary due diligence pack of all partners and beneficial owners
CSSF AML questionnaire (beneficial ownership declarations)
Business plan and projected transaction flows for medium-risk immigration/visa advisory activities
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the enhanced due diligence, provide a written AML explanation of the immigration advisory revenue model and client-source jurisdictions; in case of refusal, apply to an alternative Luxembourg bank or file a complaint with the CSSF mediation desk.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing for RCS registration and issuance of the legal entity certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed partnership deed and the prescribed RCS forms electronically, attaching the statement of the registered office address and the manager's acceptance of office; retain the RCS excerpt (extrait) evidencing the SCSp's legal personality; publication in RESA is triggered automatically upon registration.
required_dossiers: Signed partnership deed in PDF with certified e-signature
RCS standard registration form (Form B)
Proof of registered office address in Luxembourg
Beneficial owner declaration for the RBO register
Manager's identity documents and acceptance of appointment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a rectification request, correct the identified omissions within the 1-month procedural deadline by resubmitting the amended deed or forms; failure to act triggers removal from the RCS and loss of the filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and mandatory Chamber of Commerce registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RESA) and Luxembourg Chamber of Commerce (Chambre de Commerce)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The LBR automatically publishes the registration excerpt and the partnership deed in RESA; the RCS registration triggers ex officio enrollment in the National Trade and Companies Register and issuance of the Chamber of Commerce registration number; verify the extracted data and update corporate records accordingly.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate (extrait)
RESA publication confirmation
Chamber of Commerce automatic notification (no separate form needed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains errors, file a corrective act with the RCS; if the Chamber of Commerce enrollment is delayed or omitted, notify the LBR support desk to manually trigger the interconnection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT and social security registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS excerpt to the AEDT to obtain a VAT number and to the ACD to open the SCSp's corporate tax file; if the SCSp hires employees, register as an employer with the CCSS and enroll staff in the Luxembourg social security system; verify the applicability of the VAT domestic reverse charge if invoicing foreign immigration consultancies.
required_dossiers: RCS excerpt and partnership deed
Completed VAT registration form (Formulaire 564)
Corporate tax file request (ACD form)
Employer registration file for CCSS (Formular C.1)
General partner and manager identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax offices query the registrations, provide a written explanation of the SCSp's pass-through status and the place of supply rules for immigration advisory services; escalate to the respective tax office's case manager if no response within the statutory service standard.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale des classes moyennes (Department for the Middle Classes), operating through the Guichet.lu single window
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for commercial activities, required under the Law of 2 September 2011 before the SCSp commences study-abroad, university placement or immigration visa advisory operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Category C service activity – a consulting office is not listed among the classified establishments subject to the authorization regime of the Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments; no full EIA or simplified environmental screening is required for premises under 1,000 m², provided municipal building and zoning clearances are obtained
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Sanitary wastewater discharges to the municipal sewer must comply with EU Urban Wastewater Treatment Directive 91/271/EEC and Luxembourg wastewater discharge regulations; office solid waste must be separated and recovered in accordance with the Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; no VOC or industrial emissions thresholds apply to non-industrial consulting activity; confidential client documents must be destroyed through a certified waste recovery chain and handled in compliance with GDPR rules on personal data disposal

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety preventive visit and certification by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) for premises open to customers; structural load and electrical installation inspection by municipal building authorities; occupational health and workplace clearance by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workstation ergonomics, fire exits, first-aid equipment and compliance with the Law of 17 June 1994 on workplace safety and the Labour Code (Articles L.311-1 et seq.); a health-and-safety notice (affichage obligatoire) must be displayed at the registered office.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration - for direct taxes (portal: impotsdirects.public.lu); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT registration, collection and audit; Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), issues the statutory matricule number via the single digital portal MyGuichet.lu, which serves as the national TIN and VAT identifier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1 - Conclude the SCSp limited partnership agreement; notarise before a Luxembourg notary where the general partner is not a commercial company or where real-property contributions are made. Step 2 - File the incorporation dossier through MyGuichet.lu with the RCS and pay the registration fee; the RCS issues the 16-digit matricule number, which simultaneously constitutes the commercial register identifier, the direct-tax TIN and the basis for VAT identification (no separate national TIN is necessary). Step 3 - Complete the RCS 'single formalities' link, which automatically opens the direct-tax file with the ACD and transmits the data to the AEDT; the AEDT allocates the Luxembourg TVA number (format LU 12345678) normally within 2-4 weeks, without an economic-activity threshold for non-established suppliers. Step 4 - Where the SCSp has no EU establishment, appoint an approved VAT tax representative in Luxembourg who is jointly and severally liable for VAT before making any taxable supply. Step 5 - Open the operating/escrow bank account in Luxembourg and file the authorised signatory form (power of attorney) with the tax office. Step 6 - Register the employer file with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) only when a first Luxembourg employee is engaged. The SCSp files VAT, withholding and annual information returns in its own name; partners declare their allocable shares under their respective domestic tax regimes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible. The SCSp is a contractual partnership without legal personality and is fiscally transparent by default under Luxembourg domestic tax law: it is outside the scope of corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax and net wealth tax at fund level; items of income, gains and expenses flow through to each partner in proportion to their partnership interests. For indirect tax purposes the SCSp constitutes an independent taxable person (assujetti) and must charge Luxembourg VAT in its own name notwithstanding CIT transparency. A protective ATAD rule may reclassify an SCSp as a reverse hybrid taxable on its Luxembourg-source income where one or more investors are resident in a jurisdiction treating the entity as opaque.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a unitary check-the-box regime. The following elections and mechanisms are relevant: (i) optional CIT treatment for a commercial partnership that qualifies as a 'société de participations financières' (Article 175 LIR), practically inapplicable to a services business; (ii) ATAD reverse-hybrid deeming (Law of 21 December 2018 and subsequent reforms): the SCSp becomes taxable in Luxembourg on its own income, to the extent of the opaque treatment by an investor's jurisdiction; (iii) for foreign investors, the US federal check-the-box election may independently classify the SCSp (partnership or disregarded entity) on IRS Form 8832-LLC; Luxembourg will respect that result for treaty purposes; (iv) VAT elections: Article 60 VAT Law 'assujetti unique' VAT grouping with affiliated Luxembourg entities and Article 57 small-business exemption where annual turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000, although the exemption is not advisable for an advisory model claiming input VAT recovery.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law (Law of 12 February 1979, as consolidated), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (excluding VAT) for the domestic small-business exemption of Article 57 of the Luxembourg VAT Law; EUR 0 (no threshold) for any foreign-established or non-established taxable person supplying B2C services whose effective place of use or enjoyment is in Luxembourg; EU B2B services are generally reverse-charged to the Luxembourg business customer, relieving the foreign SCSp from local VAT registration, whereas exports and non-EU cross-border B2B advisory services are outside Luxembourg VAT.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Since 1 January 2022 Luxembourg mandates electronic invoicing for B2G public procurement transactions through the PEPPOL network (PEPPOL BIS Billing 3.0, UBL or CII formats). There is no national real-time fiscal clearance platform, no tax-authority pre-validation API and no digital stamping/duty mark requirement analogous to Italy's Sistema di Interscambio; the AEDT relies on periodic VAT returns and audit evidence. B2B e-invoicing is voluntary and must satisfy the authenticity-of-origin, integrity-of-content and legibility conditions of Article 90 of the VAT Law (EDI, advanced electronic signature or a reliable internal audit trail). Under the VAT-in-the-Digital-Age (ViDA) EU directive, e-invoicing and near-real-time digital transaction reporting for intra-Community supplies will become mandatory by 1 January 2030, with Luxembourg transposition to be enacted; an SCSp should therefore adopt structured electronic invoicing (XML/UBL) now to future-proof compliance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exemption with credit of input VAT) is available where: (i) goods are exported by the supplier or for the supplier's account to a non-EU destination (Article 41 Luxembourg VAT Law), provided the goods physically leave the EU within 90 days and the supplier holds the export-proof bundle; (ii) goods are supplied to a customer established in another EU Member State holding a valid VAT ID, with the goods transported out of Luxembourg within three months and recorded in an EC Sales List; and (iii) certain international transport and ancillary services. For the ISIC 7810 study-abroad and golden-visa placement services, a true 0% outcome for non-EU clients is achieved through the B2B place-of-supply rule (Article 44 Directive 2006/112/EC): advisory, placement and immigration-visa consulting services supplied to a foreign university, an overseas agency or a non-EU corporate customer are taxable where that customer is established, hence outside Luxembourg VAT. B2C supplies to non-EU private clients may likewise be excluded under the effective-use-and-enjoyment override (Article 59a of the Directive) where genuine economic use takes place entirely outside the EU; this requires contemporaneous evidence of the client's non-EU residence, the foreign visa/placement filing and the absence of Luxembourg benefit. No domestic zero-rating covers commissions on EU-bound educational placements.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: EU/Luxembourg Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ECS electronic declaration) - mandatory for any tangible promotional or study kit exported to a non-EU student; not applicable to pure consulting services but retained in the VAT audit file where export shipments occur.
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill or CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of the goods from the EU customs territory to the specified non-EU destination, dated within 90 days of the supply.

Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank account ledger evidence showing collection of the full invoice/contract amount from the non-EU counterparty in the SCSp's Luxembourg escrow or operating bank account.

Signed service agreement or placement fee contract, the foreign educational institution's acceptance or visa-support documentation, and a client declaration confirming the non-EU situs and effective use of the immigration-visa advisory service.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT carries out documentary desk checks and on-site VAT audits of export evidence; where zero-rating or non-EU outside-scope treatment is unsupported, the VAT is retrospectively re-assessed at the 17% standard rate, with monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on arrears. Negligent misstatements attract a fine of 50% of the tax at stake; intentional fraudulent arrangements (fictitious exports, circular escrow payments, sham tuition contracts or false declarations of non-EU use) are criminal tax fraud under Articles 89 et seq. of the VAT Law and the criminal provisions of the General Tax Law (Abgabenordnung), punishable by fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to five years, together with joint conviction and liability of the managing general partner, publication of the administrative enforcement act, and suspension or revocation of the statutory licence governing the immigration-paid consultancy activity. For service claims, the AEDT can demand proof of the customer's non-EU establishment and actual repatriation of the fee within the 180-day benchmark; a failure to repatriate leads to a deemed local B2C supply and penalty surcharge. In fraud cases the reassessment limitation period is extended to ten years, and clawbacks may descend on the entire chain of partners under Luxembourg VAT joint-liability principles.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) as the national central bank; Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as the integrated banking, AML/CFT, and financial-integrity supervisor. There is no separate foreign-exchange administration in Luxembourg.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area Member State. The euro is fully convertible, and the EU Treaty provisions on free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU) apply. There are no exchange controls, no capital-account approval requirements, and no statutory obstacles to profit remittance by an SCSp. Cross-border payments require normal AML/KYC compliance and, where applicable, balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL, but do not require exchange-control authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender rules, no statutory timelines for repatriation, and no mandatory conversion ratios for export or service receipts. Foreign-currency export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency or converted at the commercial discretion of the entity. Only statistical reporting obligations under BCL balance-of-payments regulations may apply to cross-border flows above applicable thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account / Operational Account / Trade Payment Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for collection of client fees and limited liquidity clearing, provided the EMI holds a valid Luxembourg e-money institution or payment-institution licence issued by the CSSF, or an EU/EEA passport into Luxembourg. Unlicensed offshore digital EMIs are not viable and will not be accepted by Luxembourg banks or notaries for an SCSp treasury structure. Legal and AML constraints under the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing require full customer due diligence, enhanced due diligence for immigration/visa services, sanctions screening, and transaction monitoring.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote client onboarding is legally permitted in Luxembourg through video-identification and e-IDAS-compliant electronic signatures where the bank's risk appetite accepts it. In practice, for a Medium-Risk Enhanced immigration/visa advisory business, most tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at least one authorised director or managing partner to attend a physical KYC interview in Luxembourg, or alternatively require a Luxembourg resident authorised signatory or a professional corporate-services provider acting as AML anchor. A notarised power of attorney, up-to-date RCS registration, and original UBO documentation materially improve onboarding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Regulatory sensitivity of immigration/visa advisory services exposing the bank to immigration fraud, human-trafficking and financial-crime risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business licence or statutory authorisation under Luxembourg and relevant jurisdiction rules; professional indemnity insurance; SCSp constitutional documents; detailed engagement letters; published fee schedule; written compliance manual incorporating risk-based CDD/EDD; monitoring framework for student placement and golden-visa applications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque SCSp ownership with non-resident limited partners or trust-like arrangements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: RCS excerpt of the SCSp; certified partnership agreement; up-to-date register of partners and ultimate beneficial owners; UBO identification under the Luxembourg AML law; notarised KYC statements for all natural-person UBOs; source-of-wealth declarations; tax-residence certificates; preliminary tax ruling, if obtained.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large escrow deposits and advance client payments without a clear beneficiary or fee-for-service chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed escrow agreement; client-specific invoices; source-of-funds evidence from bank statements; refund and indemnity provisions; detailed business-flow narrative; audit trail of payments from client to escrow account and onward disbursement; independent legal opinion on immigration/visa service deliverables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically exposed persons (PEPs), high-risk nationalities, or negative-media hits among beneficial owners or clients.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Automated and manual PEP/sanctions screening results; source-of-wealth documentation; source-of-funds evidence; negative-news and adverse-media assessment; enhanced due diligence file; senior-management risk-approval memorandum; ongoing transaction-monitoring evidence; confirmation of no prohibited activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border remittances from non-EU corridors such as China, Hong Kong, or the UAE with inconsistent payment purpose codes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Underlying visa-consulting or education-advisory contract; beneficiary’s identity and address; purpose-of-payment declaration aligned with the bank’s balance-of-payments code; source-of-funds documentation from the remitting bank; legal opinion on upstream outward-remittance compliance in the client’s jurisdiction, including PRC SAFE/ODI requirements if applicable.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for non-EU inward remittances and SEPA Credit Transfer for EU inbound euro transfers. The remitter must be the named investor or a disclosed beneficial owner and funds must originate from the investor’s own bank account. The receiving Luxembourg bank requires an investment agreement, capital-contribution schedule, and UBO/LEI information before crediting the SCSp's capital or operational account. Purpose codes must align with BCL balance-of-payments reporting, generally indicating direct-investment share capital or capital contribution to a partnership. No Luxembourg exchange-control approval is required, but statistical reporting thresholds apply to the receiving bank. For investors subject to outbound capital controls in their own jurisdiction, upstream authorisations such as PRC SAFE/ODI filing must be evidenced before remittance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For EUR disbursements to universities, visa authorities, and overseas education institutions, use SEPA Credit Transfer for EU/EEA beneficiaries and SWIFT MT103 for non-EU beneficiaries. For larger structured payments, the SCSp may use a segregated escrow account controlled by the Luxembourg bank with disbursement instructions tied to milestone invoices. Where documentary settlement is commercially required, a SWIFT MT700 Commercial Letter of Credit may be used against shipping/education-service documents, though this is uncommon for visa/study-abroad consultancy. Bank-level EUR liquidity is settled through TARGET2, ensuring irrevocable and same-day settlement for euro clearing.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forward with a CSSF-regulated Luxembourg bank or an authorised EEA credit institution, limited to underlying commercial exposure
Non-deliverable forward (NDF) on non-convertible or restricted currencies such as offshore CNY/CNH where onshore delivery is not available
FX swap between EUR and USD/GBP/CNH for period-end liquidity matching
Cross-currency interest-rate swap (CCIRS) to manage matched multi-currency assets and liabilities
Vanilla EUR/USD, EUR/GBP and EUR/CNH currency options for hedging tuition-fee and immigration-deposit cash flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts and, where applicable, management report filed and published at the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, no later than 31 July of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers court summons from the Public Prosecutor, compulsory filing proceedings, daily fines up to EUR 250, a maximum court penalty of EUR 2,500, and eventual administrative strike-off from the RCS after repeated non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership declaration update reflecting all partnership-interest transfers occurring in the preceding year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within one month of the change; for no-change years, an internal annual confirmation review is performed and documented with the annual corporate secretarial file
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file UBO changes is a criminal offence punishable by fines up to EUR 1,250 per omission (and elevated AML fines up to EUR 250,000 in aggravated cases), with repeat violations reported to the Financial Intelligence Unit.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax declaration and final VAT reconciliation for the consulting and visa-advisory services
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual-scheme taxpayers, the annual VAT return is due on or before 31 May following the tax year; where monthly or quarterly instalment declarations are used, the annual return finalises the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing or payment attracts automatic late interest of 0.8% per month, administrative fines up to EUR 10,000, and criminal sanctions for tax-evasion offences in severe or repeated cases.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds two of the three following thresholds at balance-sheet date: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average annual workforce of 50 employees. Audit is also mandatory for public-interest entities, for alternative investment funds where required by applicable fund law or CSSF authorisation, and may be contracted voluntarily by the partners.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP pursuant to the Law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts (implementing EU Directive 2013/34/EU), as amended; consolidated accounts of public-interest undertakings must comply with IFRS as endorsed by the EU; investment-fund SCSp vehicles may elect IFRS or fair-value accounting where permitted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Because the SCSp is an unincorporated special limited partnership, no separate annual UBO return exists; however, as part of Stage 5 annual secretarial maintenance the general partner must circulate an annual UBO confirmation schedule to all limited partners. Each partner must confirm current ownership percentages and disclose any direct or indirect beneficial-ownership change; the SCSp then files all modifications with the RBE within one month of the relevant transfer or event and retains the annual confirmation records in the statutory minute book and company file.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the SCSp level — the Société en Commandite Spéciale is a fully fiscally transparent Luxembourg partnership: profits are not taxed at the entity level and flow through to the partners. For comparison, a taxable Luxembourg resident company is subject to a combined 24.94% headline effective rate in Luxembourg City (17% CIT + 7% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp-level exemptions: no corporate income tax, no municipal business tax, no net wealth tax, and no subscription tax, irrespective of partner residence. Partner-level incentives available if a taxable corporate wrapper is used: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (EUR 1.2 million cost or 10% holding conditions), ATAD-compliant interest deduction (30% EBITDA cap), 30% R&D tax credit for qualifying innovation expenditure, and an outbound interest/royalty withholding tax rate of 0%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 870 (annual Declaration pour l'impot sur le revenu des collectivites — filed by the SCSp as an information/allocation return) with the profit-allocation annexes; submitted electronically to the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) via the eCDF e-filing service on myguichet.lu / impotsdirects.lu.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual — one return per partnership fiscal year, regardless of partner-level domestic reporting cycles.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The ACD filing notice prescribes the deadline; the statutory base period is six months after the fiscal year-end (LIR Art. 164), with the ACD practice of extending calendar-year filers to 31 December of the following year; a further extension of up to one additional semester is available on reasoned application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office, and ACD direct-tax file number of the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners are not identified here, but the SCSp must hold a Luxembourg tax file number and appoint a Luxembourg-based person authorized to receive tax correspondence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Address where the general partner actually exercises decision-making and where the books and records of the study-abroad/immigration advisory business are kept.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SCSp managed by a non-resident general partner, identify the Luxembourg administrative agent and evidence of substance (office, local personnel, board minutes) to avoid re-domestication of the partnership.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 — Net result of the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Global net commercial income or loss of the partnership computed under Luxembourg GAAP before profit allocation, including escrow-related fees, commission income from international student placement, and golden visa advisory fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All income is declared gross at the SCSp level; non-resident limited partners do not file this item separately in Luxembourg unless they maintain a Luxembourg permanent establishment through the SCSp activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 30 — Allocation of profits to partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Distribution of the net result to each partner per the partnership agreement's profit-sharing provisions, distinguishing general partner vs. limited partner shares and identifying any preferred-return allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Confirm each non-resident partner's tax residence and identify any Luxembourg-source fee income attributable to a Luxembourg PE; attach a partner allocation schedule for treaty claim purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of intercompany arrangements (management fees, referral commissions, IP royalties, shared services) and confirmation that arm's-length pricing documentation is in place with a functional and risk analysis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners with controlling interests must identify their ultimate parent and confirm whether group CbCR / Master File obligations are met; attach a TP summary if group revenue exceeds EUR 50 million.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the SCSp is fiscally transparent and therefore excluded from Luxembourg net wealth tax; the net wealth tax schedule is completed by the partners in their own capacity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident limited partners are not subject to Luxembourg net wealth tax on their SCSp interest absent a Luxembourg PE; no entity-level wealth tax declaration is due.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: administrative fine up to EUR 25,000 (General Tax Law (AO) Art. 168; ordinary first-offence scale EUR 150–EUR 2,500); a 10% surcharge (majoration d'impot) under AO Art. 170 where the ACD assesses ex officio; monthly default interest of 0.7% on any resulting partner-level tax; risk of immediate taxation by default and loss of the right to deduct certain expenses if the return is not produced within the prescribed time.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% — distributions from the SCSp to any partner (resident or non-resident) are not dividends and are exempt from Luxembourg withholding tax because the SCSp is a pure pass-through vehicle. Comparator: dividends from a standard Luxembourg S.a r.l. carry a 15% statutory WHT, fully relieved at 0% for qualifying EU parent-company shareholders under Directive 2011/96/EU and zero/5%/15% under most tax treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No tax-treaty reclaim is needed for SCSp distributions. For underlying withholding suffered in source states, the partner applies for relief using the foreign state's forms, attaching: (1) a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (Formulaire 430) issued by the ACD upon filing of the SCSp's annual return; (2) the partnership deed and any PPM; and (3) an ownership/economic-beneficiary statement. Reclaims filed in Luxembourg (e.g., on inbound portfolio dividends) are made with the ACD Form 700 series and must be accompanied by the home-state residence certificate and evidence of the DTA limitation; processing averages 6–18 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Outbound: 0% Luxembourg WHT on both interest and IP royalties — no statutory or treaty-based deduction at Luxembourg source. Treaties commonly preserve source-state taxing rights at 10% for interest and 5%–10% for royalties, but Luxembourg itself levies no withholding; the SCSp must nonetheless ensure that any underlying loan or IP has economic substance and a valid commercial rationale to resist GAAR re-characterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 50,000,000 — group-level annual turnover/balance-sheet threshold above which a Luxembourg taxpayer (including a transparent SCSp) must prepare and retain a full OECD Master File and Local File (ACD Circular LIR n 56/1 of 28 June 2016); MNE groups with consolidated revenue equal to or exceeding EUR 750,000,000 must file a Country-by-Country Report with the ACD.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone ESR code (unlike the UAE or Cayman) but applies an overriding anti-abuse economic-substance doctrine: the SCSp must show real premises, personnel, and risk management in Luxembourg; the general partner must document commercial rationale and decision minutes. A visa/immigration advisory business will be scrutinized for artificial profit shifting to zero-tax jurisdictions. Non-compliance triggers GAAR re-attribution (LIR Art. 6(1)), denial of treaty benefits under the MLI/PPT standard, the ATAD 30% EBITDA interest limitation, and CRS/FATCA integrity reviews.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission of partner allocation schedules; concealment of cash or crypto-paid referral fees from study-abroad/immigration clients; false declaration of the general partner's residence; backdated amendments to the partnership agreement to shift profits to a tax-haven partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine of up to EUR 250,000 or double the tax evaded, and imprisonment of up to 5 years (Luxembourg Law of 25 March 2016); administrative re-assessment plus 10% surcharge and 0.7% monthly default interest; publication of the conviction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner and any managing director are personally liable for the criminal fine and civil restitution; criminal conviction triggers cross-border travel bans, potential extradition, disqualification from holding office, and civil exposure to co-partners for the full tax shortfall.
